chunks: Three - Muhammad ibn Hammam from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Jumhur, who said: Al-Husayn ibn Rawh (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to me from Muhammad ibn Ziyad from Abu Hashim al-Ja'fari, who said: Abu Muhammad al-Hasan ibn Ali (peace be upon him) said to me:
"My grave is in Sarman; there is safety for the people of the two sides."

key_terms.أَهْلِ الْجَانِبَيْنِ: The people of the two sides

ai.seo_question: Where is the grave of Imam al-Hasan (AS) and what is its significance?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Hasan al-Askari (peace be upon him) identifies his burial place in Sarman (Samarra) as a source of divine tranquility (*aman*) for the 'people of the two sides,' a phrase often interpreted in Shia exegesis as referring to both the Jinn and humans, or the two major Islamic communities. This narration underscores the spiritual centrality of the Imam's resting place, serving as a locus of peace and intercession for all creation, thereby elevating the status of Ziyarat to the Imams as a means of attaining cosmic security.
